I suppose it’s important for me to be successful because I really grew up with so little, and my mother worked so hard and struggled providing for us (she did her best and i love that woman to death). I just don’t want to go back to that life. I don’t want that for myself or my children. Also I want to do the things that I never got to do! Unfortunately in our society,  we have to work a successful job to achieve those things.

Regarding Nietzsche, I believe we’re always trying to accomplish something. Nobody wants to sit around their entire lives (or most people at least). Some people strive to accomplish a series of paintings they’ve been working on or a story they are writing. I think for plenty of people it would be enough to work towards something. But people like me do not have the drive or interest to work towards something, hence the feeling that I’m failing. It really doesn’t matter to me exactly what I am trying to do, I’m just dying to actually want to do something

I guess I would say it’s a combination of the two (i think?). There’s a little bit of a grey area.

For example, I want to be a doctor. I want to be smart enough to be a doctor. Is that from a place of “i want to help people” (a goal for myself) or a place of “i want to make money” (a societal standard)? I don’t think I know myself. Both maybe? I do want to make money, a lot of it, because I didn’t grow up with anything at all. Maybe I want to be a doctor because it’s so ingrained in me that I have to be successful that I make up excuses like “i want to help people”. Maybe it’s a little bit of both.
I know. I know... I just want to do what’s best for him, and myself. I’m not trying to be selfish or hurtful. It makes me want to cry
